content.text:
<document id=DOC_req_years_eight>
Required: 8 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_no_dates>
Backend engineering across transactional services, most recently a
settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day. Previously worked on
payment reconciliation and inventory systems.
</document>

Rewrite the candidate summary below to match the posting requirement.

If years of experience are neither stated nor calculable, ask me for the
figure and tell me what it costs not to supply it.

response.text:
The summary gives no years of experience and no dates, so I can't state or calculate the figure. I won't guess at a number.

**How many years of backend engineering experience do you have?** If you'd rather give dates, the start year of your first backend role works too.

**What it costs to leave it out:** The posting lists 8 years as a *requirement*. Recruiters and applicant-tracking systems often screen on that number first. A summary without it:

- **May be filtered out automatically** if the ATS looks for a years figure
- **Leaves a recruiter guessing**, and a skimming reader with no number will usually assume you fall short
- **Wastes your strongest material.** The 40,000-orders-a-day pipeline is impressive, but it doesn't answer the question the posting asks first.

**Draft, ready for your number:**

> Backend engineer with **[X] years** of experience building transactional services. Most recently built and maintained a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders a day; previously developed payment reconciliation and inventory systems.

If your figure is **8 or more**, it drops straight in. If it's **under 8**, tell me and I'll rework the framing to lean on scale and domain depth.
